Stack de producción del VPS (3 apps sobre Postgres+Redis tras Caddy)
PEDIDO Frontend Static Visual Asset Set (branding + decorative backgrounds)
PWA Installability Icon Set (192px + 512px manifest icons)
Procovar VA Monogram Asset Family (PWA icons + in-app logos)

nodes.label: Desarrollo local con SQLite (DATABASE_PROVIDER=sqlite)
nodes.rationale: Development keeps SQLite (file:./prisma/dev.db) so a developer can run the API without Docker or Postgres; the Docker compose path uses PostgreSQL for anything production-like.

nodes.label: Guía de Despliegue en Windows (Procavar Pedidos)
nodes.norm_label: guia de despliegue en windows (procavar pedidos)

nodes.label: setup-windows-service.bat (instalación automática)
nodes.rationale: One-shot installer run as Administrator: installs NVM/Node/PM2/serve, builds api+front, copies to service-api/service-front, offers to delete source code as protection, and registers PM2 startup.

nodes.label: web.config rewrite para rutas React en IIS
nodes.rationale: The SPA does client-side routing, so IIS must rewrite every URL that is neither an existing file nor directory to / — otherwise deep links 404.
nodes.norm_label: web.config rewrite para rutas react en iis

nodes.label: Cambio de puerto de API exige recompilar el front
nodes.rationale: API_BASE_URL is baked into the frontend bundle at build time (front/src/config/index.ts), so moving the API off 8400 requires editing the config and running npm run build again.
nodes.norm_label: cambio de puerto de api exige recompilar el front

nodes.label: Infra del VPS 72.60.115.124 (PEDIDO docker + DELIVERY/ANALITICS systemd)
nodes.rationale: One shared VPS (also hosting ERPNext/n8n) runs all three apps; nginx on the host routes the pedidos/delivery/analitics subdomains and /api to the backends.
nodes.norm_label: infra del vps 72.60.115.124 (pedido docker + delivery/analitics systemd)

nodes.label: Secretos divergentes en el VPS (working-tree no commiteado)
nodes.rationale: The VPS compose files and .env hold real inline secrets absent from the repo (which only has placeholders). They are uncommitted working-tree changes, so git clone/checkout/reset/stash destroys them: the next up -d starts the API with a placeholder JWT secret (invalidating sessions), with no shared service key (delivery gets 401) and without Redis. It already happened once. Recommended fix: move them to a gitignored .env referenced via env_file so git never touches them.
nodes.norm_label: secretos divergentes en el vps (working-tree no commiteado)

nodes.label: BUILD_STANDALONE=1 obligatorio en el build de DELIVERY
nodes.rationale: systemd runs .next/standalone/server.js, and next.config emits output:'standalone' only when BUILD_STANDALONE=1. A plain npm run build deletes .next/standalone, so the unit fails on CHDIR/server.js and the site 502s.
nodes.norm_label: build_standalone=1 obligatorio en el build de delivery

nodes.label: Mirror de clientes PEDIDO→DELIVERY
nodes.rationale: Delivery mirrors only geolocated PEDIDO clients (without coordinates there is no delivery cost to quote), auto-synced each worker cycle rather than by a manual button, so an order created from a route can pick a client and get a price immediately.

nodes.label: Patrón source/externalId/meta (Customer igual que Order)
nodes.rationale: Reusing Order's shape — source ('pedido' vs null), externalId unique per [source, externalId] for idempotent upserts, and meta with the full payload — lets the sync delete stale mirrored rows without ever touching manually created local customers.

nodes.label: syncCustomers() en sync-queue.mjs
nodes.rationale: Upserts the mirror every cycle and deletes rows that no longer come from PEDIDO, but never deletes on a failed fetch so a transient outage cannot wipe the mirror.

nodes.label: Arquitectura event-driven (sin polling) con colas in/out
nodes.rationale: Explicit user requirement: delivery must not ask every 15s whether a new order exists; PEDIDO notifies on creation and delivery reacts. Bull queues are split by direction (in:* / out:*) so inbound and outbound flow in parallel.
nodes.norm_label: arquitectura event-driven (sin polling) con colas in/out

nodes.label: Gate DELIVERY_EVENTS (despliegue inerte + rollback)
nodes.rationale: Both slices shipped disabled: with the flag off nothing enqueues and delivery keeps the 15s poll, so the code could be deployed before cutover and rolled back by flipping one env var in both apps plus a restart.

nodes.label: SAFETY_POLL_MS (red de seguridad lenta, default 5min)
nodes.rationale: Even in event-driven mode a slow safety poll catches events lost while the worker was down; 0 disables it entirely.

nodes.label: procovar-redis publicado en 127.0.0.1:6379 para delivery nativo
nodes.rationale: Delivery runs systemd-native on the host (no container), so the dockerized Redis had to bind 127.0.0.1:6379 for it to connect. Doing so also activated R4a/R5, which had silently been running in their no-Redis fallback.
nodes.norm_label: procovar-redis publicado en 127.0.0.1:6379 para delivery nativo

nodes.label: SSE autenticado por ticket efímero (POST /orders/sse-ticket)
nodes.rationale: EventSource cannot send headers, so the stream is authorized with a short-lived ticket in the query string instead of putting the JWT in the URL.

nodes.label: SERVICE_API_KEY compartida (header x-api-key)
nodes.rationale: Must be identical in the PEDIDO api and delivery's .env; if they diverge the delivery sync gets 401.

nodes.label: Bloqueo de datos: 0 de 115 clientes con geolocalización
nodes.norm_label: bloqueo de datos: 0 de 115 clientes con geolocalizacion

nodes.label: Moneda USD/CUP con useCurrency()
nodes.rationale: Amounts are stored in USD as the single source of truth and only the display converts using Settings.cupRate; editable config inputs stay in USD because bidirectional conversion while editing introduces rounding problems.

nodes.label: Whitelist de sudo de jose (ruta completa /usr/bin/systemctl)
nodes.rationale: The sudoers entries match absolute paths, so bare `sudo systemctl` prompts for a password; jose can restart the three units and run the pedido compose files, but not nginx, git in /root, or service creation.
nodes.norm_label: whitelist de sudo de jose (ruta completa /usr/bin/systemctl)

nodes.label: Rol Supervisor con vendedores + isGlobalAdmin consistente
nodes.rationale: With zero Gestores in the branch, 130 orders were invisible; letting Supervisor carry sellers plus fixing per-branch user filters restored visibility.
nodes.norm_label: rol supervisor con vendedores + isglobaladmin consistente

nodes.label: Auto-sync de productos bloqueado (warehouse externo sin webhooks)
nodes.rationale: The warehouse is a third-party system with no webhooks, so products cannot be event-driven. It needs the devops owner to expose either a product-change webhook (ideal, making Product a global auto-updated mirror) or an updatedSince delta endpoint; otherwise only spaced pulls plus the 10-minute Redis cache.
nodes.norm_label: auto-sync de productos bloqueado (warehouse externo sin webhooks)

nodes.label: Colas out:* (Slice 3) diferidas a propósito
nodes.rationale: Outbound already has a durable queue with retries (the SyncJob table plus MAX_ATTEMPTS), so splitting out:quote / out:writeback into Bull adds little and risks the hot path.

nodes.label: Dockerizar delivery (opcional, systemd→docker)
nodes.rationale: Requested for consistency with pedido, but the container would need to reach native Postgres :5432, the warehouse VPN (10.188.x) and the api :8400 — likely network_mode: host. Not required for correctness, and jose has no compose whitelist for delivery.

nodes.label: servicio api (procovar-api, :8400)
nodes.rationale: Waits on the postgres healthcheck before starting, mounts api_uploads for persistence, and in the repo version carries only placeholder JWT secret configuration and RUN_SEED=true.

nodes.label: Dos formas de despliegue (LOCAL vs VPS)
nodes.norm_label: dos formas de despliegue (local vs vps)

nodes.label: Layout vps-deploy/ con los 3 repos como hermanos
nodes.rationale: The VPS compose builds all three projects at once, so its build contexts are relative to a parent folder holding the three clones side by side. The vps/ bundle is byte-identical in the three repos so the same stack travels versioned with each codebase.
nodes.norm_label: layout vps-deploy/ con los 3 repos como hermanos

nodes.label: Modelo LOCAL por sucursal (Windows + PM2, sin nube)
nodes.rationale: One server per branch, fully isolated and Dockerless: it works because only a single branch enters data at a time, so heavy work can run inline inside the request.
nodes.norm_label: modelo local por sucursal (windows + pm2, sin nube)

nodes.label: Flujo de costo de domicilio (pull → cotiza → writeback)
nodes.rationale: Delivery pulls orders from PEDIDO, computes warehouse→client distance times the formula using the per-SKU weight fetched over the VPN, and writes costoDomicilio back into PEDIDO over HTTP, all scoped to the branch.
nodes.norm_label: flujo de costo de domicilio (pull → cotiza → writeback)

nodes.label: Tabla SyncJob como "redis sin redis"
nodes.rationale: A DB table plus a polling worker stands in for a real queue so the local install needs no Redis; it also backs the live /sync page over SSE.

nodes.label: Guard de configuración (fórmula + punto de partida)
nodes.rationale: Quoting refuses to run until both the global formula and the branch warehouse coordinates exist, so jobs queue instead of producing wrong prices; changing either afterwards only affects new orders, leaving already-quoted ones stable.
nodes.norm_label: guard de configuracion (formula + punto de partida)

nodes.label: VPN WireGuard por sucursal (túnel al warehouse)
nodes.rationale: Each server has its own tunnel installed as a service; two tunnels on the same 10.188.2.0/24 must never be active at once because they collide.
nodes.norm_label: vpn wireguard por sucursal (tunel al warehouse)

nodes.label: Data Warehouse de pesos (10.188.2.2:3001, read-only por VPN)
nodes.rationale: Remote read-only source of per-SKU weightKg reachable only through the VPN; many products lack a weight and are quoted with 0 kg, distance pricing still applies.
nodes.norm_label: data warehouse de pesos (10.188.2.2:3001, read-only por vpn)

nodes.label: SUCURSAL_CODIGO (scoping del worker por sucursal)
nodes.rationale: In the local model it holds this branch's code so the worker only pulls its own orders; in the centralized model it is empty so one worker processes every branch.

nodes.label: Next bajo PM2 no carga .env (set -a; . ./.env; set +a)
nodes.rationale: PM2 spawns the process without Next's dotenv loading, so DATABASE_URL and friends must be exported into the shell environment before pm2 start or the app comes up unconfigured.
nodes.norm_label: next bajo pm2 no carga .env (set -a; . ./.env; set +a)

nodes.label: Migración SQLite→Postgres con export-all.mjs / import-all.mjs
nodes.rationale: Repo migrations are SQLite-shaped, so Postgres schemas are created with prisma db push and data moves via a JSON dump imported with idempotent upserts by id — no data loss and re-runnable.

nodes.label: Backfill de sucursalId antes de importar geo
nodes.rationale: The geolocation importer matches on sucursalId plus name, so if legacy orders/clients still have NULL sucursalId after the multi-branch migration the import matches nothing (0%). Order matters: backfill first, geo second.
nodes.norm_label: backfill de sucursalid antes de importar geo

nodes.label: Prisma 7 con driver adapter (prisma-node-client.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Standalone .mjs scripts can no longer construct a bare PrismaClient under Prisma 7; they must go through the driver adapter.

nodes.label: Worker procovar-delivery-sync debe estar online
nodes.rationale: It is a separate PM2 process from the web app; without it orders enqueue but nobody processes them and costoDomicilio is never computed.

nodes.label: delivery se queda en Postgres (campos Json)
nodes.rationale: Its Prisma schema uses Json columns that SQLite does not support, so unlike PEDIDO it can never be downgraded to SQLite.
nodes.norm_label: delivery se queda en postgres (campos json)

nodes.label: Build normal bajo PM2 (evitar warning de output: standalone)
nodes.rationale: standalone output is only for Docker; under PM2 the app is started with next start, and a standalone build spams delivery-error.log with a cosmetic warning that hides real errors.
nodes.norm_label: build normal bajo pm2 (evitar warning de output: standalone)

nodes.label: config.json con el sucursalId REAL de esta instalación
nodes.rationale: Copying the file from another install points at an id that does not exist in this database, and the integration silently returns 0 orders.
nodes.norm_label: config.json con el sucursalid real de esta instalacion

nodes.label: pm2 save tras añadir procesos
nodes.rationale: Unsaved processes vanish on a daemon restart or pm2 resurrect, which is how the sync worker silently disappears.

nodes.label: Modelo CENTRALIZADO en la nube (VPS, producción real)
nodes.rationale: All branches live in one place with per-branch isolation at the user level; the design must survive several branches entering data concurrently, which is what forces queues and pub/sub.
nodes.norm_label: modelo centralizado en la nube (vps, produccion real)

nodes.label: Por qué Redis (bus de mensajes + backend de colas)
nodes.rationale: Three things break under N concurrent branches: CSV import inside the request starves the Node event loop and Postgres connections; a table-polling delivery worker duplicates work once the API scales; and per-client SSE polling turns 50 viewers into ~17 queries/s. Redis converts heavy input into rate-limited queued jobs and live updates into pushed events.
nodes.norm_label: por que redis (bus de mensajes + backend de colas)

nodes.label: src/lib/redis.ts (connection + pub/sub duplicados)
nodes.rationale: maxRetriesPerRequest:null is required by BullMQ, and pub/sub needs separate duplicated connections because a subscribed connection cannot issue normal commands.

nodes.label: Cola import-csv (POST /orders/bulk responde 202 + jobId)
nodes.rationale: The endpoint keeps the same branch scoping but only enqueues and answers immediately; the row-by-row work moves to the worker with bounded concurrency and retries, and the front follows progress over SSE.

nodes.label: Servicio worker (misma imagen, node dist/worker.js)
nodes.rationale: Same image with a different command, so workers can be scaled independently of the API (docker compose up --scale worker=3).

nodes.label: Refactor a src/lib/importCore.ts (endpoint y worker comparten lógica)
nodes.rationale: Extracting mapCsvRecords/resolveSeller/processOrderRecord out of routes/orders.ts avoids duplicating the import logic between the request path and the worker: behaviour is unchanged, only where it runs changes.
nodes.norm_label: refactor a src/lib/importcore.ts (endpoint y worker comparten logica)

nodes.label: SSE de pedidos por Redis Pub/Sub (canal orders:new)
nodes.rationale: Replaces per-client 3s Postgres polling with push, and is the only way multiple API instances see each other's writes; the subscriber still filters by sucursalId so isolation is preserved.
nodes.norm_label: sse de pedidos por redis pub/sub (canal orders:new)

nodes.label: Cola domicilios (BullMQ, reemplaza el polling de SyncJob)
nodes.rationale: Producer enqueues on order creation instead of the worker polling; a limiter keeps the deliberate slow pace while adding real retries. No data migration needed — pending orders are re-enqueued by an initial sweep of orders without cost.
nodes.norm_label: cola domicilios (bullmq, reemplaza el polling de syncjob)

nodes.label: Cola db-restore (restaurar backup de otro server)
nodes.norm_label: cola db-restore (restaurar backup de otro server)

nodes.label: Cache en Redis (pesos del warehouse y reportes pesados)
nodes.rationale: Short-TTL cache keyed by sucursalId+filters for reports (invalidated on import) and a 10-15 min shared cache of the weight map so every delivery worker does not re-download the catalog over the VPN.
nodes.norm_label: cache en redis (pesos del warehouse y reportes pesados)

nodes.label: Concurrencia acotada (IMPORT_CONCURRENCY, limiter de BullMQ)
nodes.rationale: Ten simultaneous imports must not kill Postgres: N run and the rest wait in the queue, with the DB connection_limit (or PgBouncer) as a second safety belt.

nodes.label: Reverse proxy sin buffering para SSE (flush_interval -1)
nodes.rationale: A buffering proxy or short read timeout silently breaks the event stream; X-Accel-Buffering: no covers the nginx case.
nodes.norm_label: reverse proxy sin buffering para sse (flush_interval -1)

nodes.label: Cutover a centralizado (consolidar históricos sin perder datos)
nodes.rationale: One procovar_pedido database with a Sucursal row per branch; each local server's backup is restored with idempotent upserts so histories merge without duplicating orders, config.json stops pinning a branch (it comes from the user), and isolation is verified by logging in as users of two branches.
nodes.norm_label: cutover a centralizado (consolidar historicos sin perder datos)

nodes.label: Aislamiento por sucursal (usuario vs Super Admin)
nodes.norm_label: aislamiento por sucursal (usuario vs super admin)

nodes.label: Bundle real (sync-queue.mjs) vs upgrade futuro a BullMQ
nodes.rationale: The shipped bundle runs the current DB-backed sync worker, while the `worker: node dist/worker.js` service in the inline YAML is the future BullMQ upgrade. Redis is already in the bundle so enabling it later needs no compose edit.
nodes.norm_label: bundle real (sync-queue.mjs) vs upgrade futuro a bullmq

nodes.label: servicio postgres (2 bases via initdb)
nodes.rationale: initdb scripts only run on the first initialization of the volume, so the two app databases are created once at bootstrap.

nodes.label: servicio redis (appendonly yes)
nodes.rationale: appendonly persistence so queued jobs survive restarts; every producer/consumer reaches it as redis://redis:6379 on the compose network.

nodes.label: servicio pedido-api (Express + Prisma 7, :8400)
nodes.rationale: Entrypoint runs prisma db push and seeds only when RUN_SEED is true; production sets it false to avoid overwriting real data. JWT secret configuration must stay stable or all sessions are invalidated.

nodes.label: servicio delivery (Next standalone :3000)
nodes.rationale: Built with BUILD_STANDALONE=1 and starts with prisma migrate deploy then node server.js; it errors out at boot if the JWT secret is missing because login requires it.

nodes.label: servicio delivery-sync (worker Dockerfile.worker)
nodes.rationale: Needs its own image because the standalone web image does not ship the worker's dependencies; it gets DELIVERY_URL so it can call the quoting endpoint.

nodes.label: servicio analitics-api (FastAPI, alias de red backend)
nodes.rationale: The analitics front's nginx proxies /api/ to the literal host `backend`, so the service declares that network alias; it reads PEDIDO's database directly for analytics.
nodes.norm_label: servicio analitics-api (fastapi, alias de red backend)

nodes.label: servicio front (procovar-front, host 5001→5000)
nodes.rationale: Host port 5001 because :5000 is already taken by another app on the VPS; the host nginx proxies the pedidos vhost to 5001.

nodes.label: Shell SPA de PROCOVAR (index.html, /src/main.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Mobile-oriented shell (viewport-fit=cover, user-scalable=0) describing the product as an offline-first commercial management tool.

nodes.label: Soft Pastel Gradient Background Aesthetic (Blue/Violet Blur Blobs)
nodes.norm_label: soft pastel gradient background aesthetic (blue/violet blur blobs)

nodes.label: Procovar Brand Identity (VA Monogram, Deep Navy Blue)
nodes.norm_label: procovar brand identity (va monogram, deep navy blue)

nodes.label: logo - copia.png - Procovar Monogram Only (Duplicate Asset)
nodes.norm_label: logo - copia.png - procovar monogram only (duplicate asset)
